title: Bound all single-port releases in the fixed BIT chart quotient
body:
All 111 whole-port projections have negative optimistic signed changes in the retained 656-component quotient with original nesting and fixed projected paid omissions. The strongest first-trial upper is −7.955161470836255 for port 89. The separate port-89-plus-helper-660 case has upper −7.6420789376396004. The bill includes the lost caller targets, native paid changes and every helper debit in scope.

## Task and overlap

The fixed native graph is #7830, with caller grading from #7952 `755fcee748d4e90feda281f27d06e7bc66ecf954` and prior protected-geometry graph extraction from #7910. The Round 7 pure-zero closure #7974 keeps all main ports, and the partial-port caller #7977 tests a different interface. The scoped task is the #7852 follow-up at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, based on `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` and #7830 `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive gives exact source identities and complete assumptions.

## Validation

Verify the extracted SHA256SUMS and replay `windows.py`, `optimize.py`, and `verify.py` under Python 3.12 as specified. The clean-copy run took about 31 seconds. A separate incidence and tariff enumeration agrees and checks the 678/677 surviving rows in both directions.

## Open next questions

Extract a new cochart quotient from the actual punctured and recompiled packet tape. Its components may split, and its new constraints and prices need independent replay.

## Credit
